newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls on Chechnya to allow diplomat back.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls on Chechnya to allow diplomat back.

text.p: The United States is calling on Chechnya's outgoing provisional president to reverse a decision to expel the head of a mission of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

The outgoing Chechen government of Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev said on Tuesday that Swiss diplomat Tim Guldimann was being expelled. The self-styled foreign ministry criticised him for calling Chechnya part of the Russian Federation.
But State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said it was difficult to accept Yandarbiyev's explanation as Guldimann's statement reflected long-standing OSCE policy and international law.
"We call upon President Yandarbiyev to immediately reverse his decision and allow Guldimann to return to Chechnya," Burns said in a statement issued on Tuesday evening.
He said the move was "especially disappointing after all sides have so successfully collaborated in good faith to stage the recent presidential and parliamentary elections".
Russia withdrew its remaining forces from Chechnya last month, marking the end of a military campaign launched in 1994 to crush a Chechen drive for independence.
Chechnya is now seeking full independence but Moscow refuses any concession on sovereignty.
